claims.claim: Chambers (1987; abstract), also in southern Québec, found the minimum depth of submerged plants equal to the depth of wave mixing (r = 0.86)
claims.note: No full text. The abstract agrees: the minimum depth of occurrence (zmin) along undisturbed shores of four southern Quebec lakes correlated with the depth of surface wave mixing (zw, calculated from wind velocity and fetch), r = 0.86, P < 0.001, slope not different from 1.0 and intercept not different from 0 (t-tests, P > 0.10). The paper's '(abstract)' tag is accurate; 'equal to' is a fair reading of slope 1, intercept 0.

claims.claim: the shallowest submerged plants sit at the depth the waves stir the bed to: minimum depth vs wave-mixing depth r 0.86, slope 1 and intercept 0
claims.note: The numbers agree with the abstract. What the full text must settle: how zw was computed (which wind — mean, maximum or a design storm — and which wave formula), since the model's zWave is the depth where the orbital velocity of fetch-limited waves at a 10 m/s 'storm' wind falls to 0.10 m/s at the bed (STORM_U, U_CRIT), which may not be Chambers' zw; and the lakes' fetch range and n.
